title: Class 12 Student Found With Severe Burns at Delhi School Dies
excerpt: Police, a crime team and an education department inquiry are examining how an approximately 18-year-old student was found with severe burns behind the guard room at a Krishna Nagar government school on Saturday.
body:
• An approximately 18-year-old Class 12 student was found with severe burn injuries behind the guard room at a government school in Krishna Nagar, East Delhi, on Saturday and was declared dead at hospital.
  • Delhi Police said a crime team inspected the scene, a fire brigade attended, and materials recovered from the spot and from the student's school bag are being examined.
  • Delhi Education Minister Ashish Sood visited the school, ordered an inquiry and said action would follow the findings, according to ANI and other reports.
  • Police said the circumstances are still being examined and no motive has been officially confirmed; readers in distress can call Tele-MANAS on 14416 or the Kiran helpline on 1800-599-0019.

An approximately 18-year-old Class 12 student died on Saturday after she was found with severe burn injuries on the campus of a government school in Krishna Nagar, in Delhi's Shahdara district, police and officials said. The student was found behind the school guard room after a Police Control Room call reporting a fire at the school, according to Delhi Police.

Police staff from Krishna Nagar police station reached the school promptly, officials said. A fire brigade team also attended. The student was taken to hospital, where she was declared dead, according to reporting by Jagran and PTI inputs. Police have not officially confirmed a motive.

What police say happened

Delhi Police said in a statement quoted by IANS: "Upon receipt of the information, police staff from PS Krishna Nagar promptly reached the spot, where an approximately 18-year-old female student of Class 12th was found in a burnt condition behind the school guard room."

https://x.com/ANI/status/2113912116554109172

Jagran reported, citing police, that the student had taken a pass after a class period saying she was going to drink water, and that staff and students rushed to the area after hearing screams minutes later. That sequence has not been set out in the police statement quoted by IANS, and investigators are still establishing the sequence of events.

"The circumstances leading to the incident are being examined, and further enquiry is in progress."

— Delhi Police, quoted by IANS

Investigation under way

A Delhi Police crime team was called to the school to inspect the scene and collect evidence, police said. "During preliminary proceedings, certain materials were recovered from the spot and the deceased girl's school bag," officials told IANS. The nature of those materials has not been officially confirmed, police added, and they are being examined as part of the investigation.

Jagran reported that police recovered notes and a lighter from the student's bag. Police quoted in the IANS report did not confirm the contents of the bag. The Videshi is reporting only what officials have confirmed on the record: that materials were recovered and are being examined, and that further details are expected as the enquiry continues.

Fire Officer Anoop Singh said one fire tender reached the spot and the cause of the fire had not yet been ascertained, according to ANI reporting carried by Daily Prabhat.

Education minister orders inquiry

Delhi Education and Sports Minister Ashish Sood visited the Government Sarvodaya Kanya Vidyalaya in Krishna Nagar on Saturday, sought details from school management and police, and ordered an inquiry, ANI reported. Krishna Nagar MLA Anil Goyal was also present.

Sood described the death as deeply distressing and a matter of serious concern, said the school management had handed all available evidence to Delhi Police, and emphasised that the priority was a fair and thorough investigation to establish the facts. Appropriate action would be taken in accordance with the law based on the findings, he said, according to ANI and Careers360.

Support and what happens next

The death has raised concern among teachers, students and residents, and the school and police faced questions on Saturday about supervision and support on campus. Those questions can only be answered once the police enquiry and the education department inquiry are complete. Police said they are examining available evidence and witness accounts, and officials said further details would emerge as the investigation progresses.

If you or someone you know is in distress, help is available in India through Tele-MANAS on 14416 or 1800-891-4416, the Kiran mental health helpline on 1800-599-0019, and Sumaitri in Delhi on 011-23389090. Those numbers were listed in coverage of this incident by Jagran.
